issues.description: Method Stock.take(String): the problem statement UML and the solution implementation declare Stock.take(String) to return an int (using -1 to indicate missing/insufficient ingredient), but the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) returning boolean and uses true/false semantics. This mismatch concerns the same method name and parameter list across artifacts and will prevent students from implementing or compiling checkOrderReady() logic that relies on integer return values (e.g., comparing to -1) and restoring consumed ingredients using integer-based semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's Stock.take(String) method signature and implementation to return an int consistent with the UML and the solution: return -1 when the ingredient is missing or its quantity is insufficient, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the new quantity. Update any template comments or examples accordingly so that checkOrderReady() and other code can compare the return value to -1 and behave the same as in the reference solution.

issues.description: Concept: the Stock.take operation (removing/consuming one unit of an ingredient from stock). Problem statement (UML) specifies Stock.take(String): int. Template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) declares public boolean take(String ingredient). Solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) declares public int take(String ingredient) and uses -1 to signal missing/out-of-stock. SealSaloon implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java in the solution) calls stock.take(x) and checks for -1. This mismatch (boolean vs int return and differing failure signaling) breaks the conceptual mapping: students reading the UML and solution will expect an int-returning take method with -1 on failure, but the template's boolean signature will either cause compile errors or force students to change the template in ways not described by the problem, creating significant confusion and blocking correct implementation of SealSaloon.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Stock.take contract across all artifacts. Prefer updating the template to match the UML and solution: change the template method signature to public int take(String ingredient) and implement it to return the new quantity on success and -1 when the ingredient is missing or out of stock. Update any template/internal callers accordingly. Alternatively, if a boolean contract is preferred, update the UML and solution to use boolean and adjust failure handling consistently; however, aligning the template to the existing UML/solution (int with -1) is recommended to avoid changing the shown solution logic.
